subject: Post-demo: Nimbus Health TCO & token-econ test plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@nimbus.health>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Oct 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Nimbus Health TCO & token-econ test plan

Hi Alex / team,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — great context on your chat + batch scoring mix. I pulled a short recap and proposed next steps so we can align on a focused competitive TCO + unit-econ test.

Recap (from our side):
- Current infra: you mentioned most production traffic runs on GCP/Vertex with a mix of streaming chat (approx 60%) and batched scoring (40%).
- SLO: target 95th tail latency <= 300ms for chat flows; batch jobs can tolerate higher latency but need throughput predictability.
- Key asks: per-1M token cost comparisons (hosted vs hyperscaler managed endpoints), batching sensitivity (batch sizes 1/8/16), and cache hit-rate impact for short-lived session prefixes.

What we propose to validate (short list):
1) Unit-econ run: synthetic 1M-token workload in two modes — low-latency streaming (micro-batches) and high-throughput batching. Produce per-1M token cost, average and 95th latency, and GPU utilization.
2) Cache sensitivity matrix: run with prefix caching enabled at simulated session reuse rates (10%, 30%, 60%) to show token-savings and tail-latency effect.
3) Hyperscaler baseline: mirror the same workload against their Vertex endpoint (your baseline) for apples-to-apples.
4) Quantized/model-variant comparison: run the same runs on standard FP16 and 4-bit quantized variant (where possible) to capture cost deltas and any quality notes.

Requests from you: can you share a small sample trace (1k - 10k requests) representative of chat and batch scoring? That will let us seed the harness rather than guessing traffic patterns.

Attached: redwood_vs_hyperscaler_ratecard.pdf (high-level rate card)

Suggested owners & timeline:
- Ben to own per-1M token cost model and hyperscaler baseline (ben) — start Monday 10/12.
- Tessa to spin up test harness and run the batches + cache matrix (tessa) — target initial runs by 10/15.
- Rishi to assist on latency SLO tuning and kernel/runtime knobs (rishi).

Next steps: Alex, if you can drop the sample traces or a Drive link, we’ll queue the runs and send a proposed test matrix before we execute. Planning goal: deliver a short deck and numbers by 10/20.

Thanks —
Marissa
---
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Nimbus Health TCO & token-econ test plan

Thanks Marissa — I’ll take the cost model. A couple quick clarifying Qs before I start:
- Which model family should we baseline on (you mentioned Llama-3 style / gpt-like); assume the 8k context variant unless you say otherwise?
- For batching sensitivity, confirm we should run at batch sizes: 1, 8, 16 (micro-batch and larger micro-batch sim).
- Any hard constraints on memory/quantization for the test (e.g., you won't allow 3-bit or custom kernels)?

I’ll draft a simple spreadsheet with per-1M token math for: tokens/sec, GPU-hours, infra cost, and add a delta for cache hit rates per scenario. Expect preliminary numbers by 10/14.

-ben

Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai
(attachment: token-econ-cost-template.xlsx)

From: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@nimbus.health>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Nimbus Health TCO & token-econ test plan

Marissa — thanks for the clear plan. I’ve uploaded a 7k-request sample trace set here: https://drive.google.com/nimbus-sample-traces (short JSONL with timestamps, prompt lengths, response lengths). Key clarifications:
- Model: we are using an open checkpoint derivative (16384 context) on Vertex today; for your baseline please use an 8k electable variant so we can see the delta.
- Workload mix: ~60% interactive chat (average response length ~120 tokens), 40% batch scoring (avg response 400 tokens).
- Session behavior: chat sessions are sticky for 10–12 turns; prefix reuse is common for personalization.

I’ll also add Samir from our infra team (cc’ed separately) to help grant any temporary Vertex project access if you need to run native baselines.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we’re particularly interested in the cache-hit sensitivity and whether batching yields better cost without blowing past our latency SLOs.

—Alex
Alex Gomez
Head of AI Engineering, Nimbus Health
alex.gomez@nimbus.health
(attachment: nimbus_sample_traces.jsonl)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@nimbus.health>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Nimbus Health TCO & token-econ test plan

Looping in a short test plan and timeline — I’ll own execution. High-level:

Test plan (v1):
- Harness: replay supplied JSONL traces against two endpoints: (A) Redwood hosted/dedicated (we’ll use our hosted with quantized and FP16 variants) and (B) Vertex managed endpoint (we’ll run against a sandbox project, Samir to provide creds).
- Runs: for each endpoint / model variant run: streaming mode (batch size 1, emulate streaming) and batched mode (batch sizes 8 and 16). Run sufficient iterations to cover ~1M tokens per scenario.
- Cache matrix: simulate prefix reuse at 10%, 30%, 60% with a short TTL to observe hit-rate and effect on tokens saved.
- Metrics captured: total tokens, GPU-hours, per-1M token $ cost, avg latency, p95/p99 latency, batch hit-rate, memory footprint, and any quality diffs (basic perplexity & spot human checks).

Artifacts we’ll produce:
- A short spreadsheet with per-1M token economics and assumptions (cost math + hardware unit prices).
- A small slide deck summarizing deltas with recommended config (batching, cache policy, quantization).
- Raw logs and a reproducible script set (token-econ-test-scripts.tar.gz).

Timeline:
- 10/12: finalize test matrix (this email)
- 10/13–10/15: run baseline experiments
- 10/16–10/17: collect results and sanity checks
- 10/20: send deck + numbers to Nimbus and schedule a readout

Open questions:
- Samir — can you confirm Vertex sandbox access by EOD 10/12?
- Alex — confirm that the 8k model variant is acceptable for the baseline; if you insist on 16k we will add that as a follow-up run but it will add time/cost.

I’ll start the harness later today and post progress logs to the shared Drive link.

Thanks —
Tessa

Tessa Morgan
Performance Engineering, Redwood Inference
tessa@redwood.ai
(attachment: token-econ-test-scripts.tar.gz)

Perfect — thanks all for the quick alignment. A couple small asks before we kick off:
- Ben: please include a per-1M token row and a per-100k embedding row (they use embeddings in a side pipeline).
- Tessa: please add a short canary plan — one small progressive rollout of the Redwood config (so we can validate latency under production-like request jitter before scaling).
- Rishi: flag any runtime knobs early (KV cache TTLs, early exit hyperparams) so Ben can model their cost impact.

Alex — we’ll aim to have the deck and numbers by 10/20 and can run a 30–45 min readout with your infra and product folks. If anything changes on your side (traces, access), drop it to the Drive link and ping me.

Marissa
